travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise increased cautionin Egypt due to terrorism, crime, and health. Some areas have increased risk. 

The U.S. Embassy has limited ability to help dual national U.S.-Egyptian citizens who are arrested or detained.
Egyptian law considers dual citizens to be solely Egyptian citizens.

healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Egypt. Emergency numbers (122/123/180), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.

connectivity.simOptions: Vodafone Egypt, Orange, or Etisalat prepaid SIMs at airport arrivals hall. Need passport. Data plans very cheap — ~50 EGP for 10GB.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels and many cafes in Cairo and tourist areas. Quality can be unreliable. Limited in Upper Egypt and desert areas.
connectivity.bestOption: Vodafone Egypt prepaid SIM at Cairo airport — counters open 24/7. Best coverage nationwide. eSIM via Airalo as alternative.

cultural.tipping: Expected everywhere. 10-15% at restaurants. Tip guides, drivers, hotel staff. Baksheesh (small tips) is part of daily life — carry small bills.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress, especially for women. Cover shoulders and knees, particularly at mosques. Women should bring a headscarf for mosque visits. Men should wear long pants at religious sites.
cultural.greetings: Handshake common between same gender. Men should wait for a woman to extend her hand first. 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you) is the standard greeting.
taboos: Using left hand to eat or pass items
Showing the soles of your feet
Photography of military installations or government buildings
Drinking alcohol in public during Ramadan
cultural.haggling: Expected and essential at bazaars, markets, and with taxi drivers. Start at 25-40% of asking price. Take your time — haggling is a social ritual.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa on arrival (USD $25) or e-Visa. UK, EU also eligible for visa on arrival. Single entry, 30 days.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-April (cooler). December-February most pleasant. Avoid June-August (extreme heat 40°C+). Ramadan dates vary — plan accordingly.

hospitals.name: As-Salam International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best hospital for tourists in Cairo. English-speaking staff, accepts international insurance.

immediate: Drink 3-4 liters of water per day
Wear loose, light-colored clothing and sun protection
Avoid prolonged exposure when temperatures exceed 40°C
after: Seek medical care for signs of heat stroke: hot dry skin, confusion
